Gross
grōs
adj. (thick, dense, fat; rendering Hebrew araphel, thick darkness, Greek pachuno, to make fat)
Latin grossus, thick. Isaiah's gross darkness is the dense cloud; the gross heart of Matthew 13 is a heart grown fat.

Biblical Definition

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee” (Isa 60:2). The Lord quoting Isaiah: “this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed” (Mat 13:15), and Paul to the Jews at Rome: “the heart of this people is waxed gross” (Act 28:27). Jeremiah: “Give glory to the LORD your God, before he cause darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains, and, while ye look for light, he turn it into the shadow of death, and make it gross darkness” (Jer 13:16).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines gross as thick, bulky; coarse, rude; stupid, dull; whole, entire, as the gross sum.

expand to see more

GROSS, a. Thick; bulky; particularly applied to animals; fat; corpulent.

2. Coarse; rude; rough; not delicate.

3. Stupid; dull; as a gross heart.

4. Whole; entire; as the gross sum, or gross amount.

Key Scripture

Mat 13:15 — "For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them."

Isa 60:2 — "For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee."

Act 28:27 — "For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them."

Jer 13:16 — "Give glory to the LORD your God, before he cause darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains, and, while ye look for light, he turn it into the shadow of death, and make it gross darkness."

Modern Corruption

A heart waxed gross is blamed on the preaching, and the Lord said the people had closed their own eyes.

expand to see more

Matthew 13:15 is the reason the Lord spoke in parables, and it is a description of a heart, not a method. The heart waxed gross — grown fat, thick, insensible — the ears dull, and then the clause that fixes responsibility: their eyes they have closed. The grossness is not something done to them but something they did, and the parables were the judgment that fitted it: light enough for the seeing, darkness enough for those who had chosen not to see. Paul quotes the same verse over the Jews of Rome at the end of Acts, and turns to the Gentiles. Isaiah 60:2 is the other grossness: darkness covering the earth, gross darkness the people — and the LORD arising upon Zion in it, so that the thicker the dark the more visible the glory. The church has never shone in daylight.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew araphel (H6205), thick darkness, gloom; Greek pachuno (G3975), to make thick, fat, gross.

expand to see more

Hebrew araphel (H6205) — gross darkness, thick cloud; Isaiah 60:2, Jeremiah 13:16, Exodus 20:21.

Greek pachuno (G3975) — to make gross, fat; Matthew 13:15, Acts 28:27 only.

Usage

"“This people's heart is waxed gross… and their eyes they have closed” — done by them, not to them."

"“Gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee” — the glory most visible in the thickest dark."

"“Give glory to the LORD your God, before he cause darkness” — Jeremiah's while-there-is-time."
